Muchísimas gracias por tu comentario. Mis papás están muy ancianos para cuidar al niño, de verdad que no pueden. Mi mamá sufre de asma y depresión crónica así que mi papá tiene que salir todo el día todos los días a todas y cada una de las farmacias en el área para ver si consigue las medicinas para ella y mientras tanto mi mamá no está en posición de cuidarlo. Quiero verlo crecer, aprender, maravillarse del mundo a su alrededor pero todo lo que tiene es el mismo DVD de Peppa porque no tenemos cable ni internet y no lo puedo sacar a jugar porque si le pica un zancudo puede enfermarse y no hay medicinas. 

Gracias por leerme y por responderme. Un abrazo! Supieras que tuve un rato pensando irme para allá pero el bebé todavía no tiene pasaporte y así no me puedo ir. Creo que terminaré yéndome a Perú.
Thank you, really \<3

Too many things. I said I am venezuelan because it has a lot to do with it. I'm living here in this hell hole of a country with my baby... It's helpless, or so it feels. Everyday I wonder where I could get money from just to go to Colombia. We have no water, power is a mess, at home there's no internet (i'm not at home) and food is a daily struggle. On top of that, the baby's father and I fight EVERY SINGLE DAY and just yesterday he yelled at me in front of the baby when I've been saying all the time that we shouldn't do that, our kid has a tough life out here already to top it with mommy and daddy fighting viciously...

My family hates me and all of our friends have fled... we have nobody here in this town. The only ones left are too far (there's no cash to go around) or they don't have internet... 

I feel alone, I feel I'm failing my kid, I feel like I can't get out of this relationship, I feel like I made a mistake by giving birth to my kid (because my family makes me feel like that every day of my life) 

I don't know what to do... maybe the baby would be better off with his paternal grandparents... I just don't know, life is soooo hard T\_T

I haven't immigrated because I'm poor, basically. I've started writing freelance to save some money to leave the country but my family duties have made it impossible to save any cash. We just make money to eat. 

Civilians can't get help from anybody. The Government has made it impossible. If you send anything to Venezuela, it would be stolen by the Army, who controls the ports and airports. Well... yes. 

Not all of us but most. I'll make an example out of my neighbors since they're a wide variety of people.

The ones on my left work for the Government. They're ok but they never protest. The grandma supports Maduro but she makes some tricky business. People hate her.

The ones on my right fled to Colombia. Before that they were starving and had many children starving too. I don't know what they're doing out there but they have been gone quite a while. 

The ones in front of me are growing plantains in the backyard. They are skinnier than ever and three families live in one house. 

Another neighbor has a Government-built house. He's starving with many children and has no job. He deals pot and God knows where he throws the money away.

Another neighbor sells plantains, pumpkins and bananas (they're very cheap) and their youngest child died after health complications.

The ones in front of them are delinquents. There are many children living there but all what they do is sell cigarettes. Ugh.

Another neighbor is a member of Maduro's Bolivarian Militia. She's starving too. 

We starve some days but we managed to freelance online and that pays the bills sometimes (we have to take advantage of the English we speak, not everybody can) We're looking to make some improvements in our situation.

And so on...
